pharm: Inhibits PARP-1, PARP-2, and PARP-3 enzymes involved in DNA single-strand break repair, causing PARP-DNA complexes ('trapping'), stalled replication forks, double-strand breaks, and synthetic-lethal cell death in tumors deficient in homologous recombination repair (e.g., BRCA-mutant cancers).

summary: Rucaparib is an oral inhibitor of PARP-1, -2, and -3 used to treat certain BRCA-mutated or homologous-recombination-deficient cancers, including maintenance treatment of recurrent ovarian/fallopian/primary peritoneal cancer in patients responding to platinum chemotherapy and BRCA-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. By inhibiting and trapping PARP on DNA, it exploits synthetic lethality in tumors that cannot repair DNA by homologous recombination. The most clinically important risks are myelosuppression (anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia) and the rare but serious development of myelodysplastic syndrome/acute myeloid leukemia (MDS/AML), which mandates regular blood-count monitoring and discontinuation if MDS/AML is confirmed. It is genotoxic and embryo-fetal toxic, requiring contraception, and is dosed 600 mg twice daily with or without food.
indications: Maintenance treatment of recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer in adults in complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy
Treatment of deleterious BRCA-mutated (germline and/or somatic) advanced ovarian cancer in patients treated with two or more prior chemotherapies (per approved labeling)
Treatment of BRCA-mutated (germline and/or somatic) metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) in patients who have progressed on androgen-receptor-directed therapy and a taxane

moa: Rucaparib inhibits poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase enzymes PARP-1, PARP-2, and PARP-3, which are critical for recognizing and repairing DNA single-strand breaks via the base-excision repair pathway. Inhibition prevents repair and traps PARP-DNA complexes at sites of damage, blocking replication forks and converting single-strand breaks into cytotoxic double-strand breaks during replication. In cells with deficient homologous recombination repair (such as BRCA1/2-mutant tumors), these double-strand breaks cannot be accurately repaired, producing synthetic lethality and selective tumor-cell death. This DNA-damaging mechanism also underlies its genotoxicity, myelosuppression, and risk of secondary myeloid malignancy.

absolute: Known severe hypersensitivity to rucaparib or excipients
relative: Pre-existing significant cytopenias or bone marrow reserve compromise
Prior MDS/AML or features suggestive of it
Severe renal or moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment (limited data)
monitor: Complete blood counts monthly and as clinically indicated
Signs of MDS/AML (prolonged or worsening cytopenias)
Pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal data, rucaparib can cause fetal harm. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Females of reproductive potential must use effective contraception during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose. Verify pregnancy status before initiating.
lact: There are no data on the presence of rucaparib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for patients with mild to moderate renal impairment (creatinine clearance >=30 mL/min). Rucaparib has not been studied in patients with severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease; use with caution if at all.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for patients with mild hepatic impairment (total bilirubin <=ULN and AST > ULN, or bilirubin 1-1.5x ULN). Rucaparib has not been studied in patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment.

major: Other myelosuppressive agents - additive bone marrow suppression
Warfarin (CYP-dependent narrow-therapeutic-index substrate) - rucaparib inhibits CYP1A2/CYP2C9/CYP2C19/CYP3A; monitor INR closely
moderate: CYP1A2 substrates (e.g., caffeine, tizanidine, duloxetine) - rucaparib may increase exposure
CYP2C9 substrates (e.g., phenytoin) and CYP2C19 substrates - increased exposure possible
P-glycoprotein substrates (e.g., digoxin) - rucaparib inhibits P-gp; monitor
MATE1/MATE2-K substrates (e.g., metformin) - increased exposure possible
minor: Effect of CYP inducers/inhibitors on rucaparib itself is limited
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal modestly affects pharmacokinetics without clinical significance.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; advise moderation during cytopenias or intercurrent illness.
interactions.diagnostics: Can elevate serum creatinine (via transporter inhibition, not necessarily reflecting reduced GFR), ALT/AST, and cholesterol.

counsel: Take two tablets twice a day, about 12 hours apart, with or without food
This medicine can lower your blood counts - keep all appointments for blood tests and report fever, unusual bruising, bleeding, or extreme tiredness
It can harm an unborn baby - use effective birth control during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose; men should also use condoms per advice
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after your last dose

pk: Antitumor effect over weeks; steady state in ~1 week
pearls: PARP inhibitor exploiting synthetic lethality in BRCA-mutated / HR-deficient tumors
Most serious risk is treatment-related MDS/AML - monitor CBC monthly and discontinue permanently if confirmed
Myelosuppression is dose-limiting; manage with interruption, dose reduction (600->500->400->300 mg BID), or stopping
Strongly embryo-fetal toxic and genotoxic - contraception during and 6 months after; no breastfeeding
Raises serum creatinine by inhibiting renal transporters (MATE1/OCT2) without truly lowering GFR - interpret cautiously
Inhibits multiple CYP enzymes - monitor warfarin INR and other narrow-index substrates
missed: If you miss a dose or vomit after a dose, do not take an extra dose. Take the next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Do not make up missed doses.
overdose: There is no specific antidote and no established treatment for rucaparib overdose. In the event of overdose, discontinue the drug, institute general supportive measures, monitor blood counts and organ function, and manage symptomatically.
